newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac shares run to record high.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac shares run to record high.

text.p: Shares in Westpac Banking Corp jumped to a record high after the bank announced an on-market share buyback of up to 85 million shares or about five percent of its ordinary capital, brokers said.
Prior to the announcement, Westpac shares were trading at A$7.15, down three cents on Friday's close, but they surged to A$7.31 shortly after.

"The buyback will satisfy a couple of things," said a Brisbane-based dealer. "There was a feeling they were a bit overcapitalised so they either had to buy something or give it back to shareholders," he said, adding that the buyback would benefit earnings per share as well as provide price support.
"I think it should be positive in terms of earnings per share and I guess people are thinking it gives a bit of underlying support to the share price for a while," he said.
Others in the market agreed, adding that takeover speculation was already providing solid support for the bank.
"That (buyback) certainly does always help the stock but also, the fact is there is still plenty of rumours running around about a takeover," said dealer Paul Ford of Shaw Stockbroking.
By 2.40 p.m. (0340 GMT), Westpac shares were up 13 cents at A$7.31 after touching an intraday and record high of A$7.35 on turnover of 1.78 million shares.
